cues.text: Your app emits events.
The rest of your stack expects webhooks.
Which means retries. Signing. Health checks. Every time.
So teams build it: a Redis queue, retry crons, signing code, dashboards, alerts.
And events still quietly get lost.
With Sparrow, it's just Postgres.
Sparrow: webhook delivery you run yourself.
Let's follow one event, item.shipped, through three nights.
cues.say: Let's follow one event, item dot shipped, through three nights.

cues.text: The happy path. The night the partner went dark. And the Tuesday you shipped a bug.
Night one. Your warehouse app pushes item.shipped: one POST.
cues.say: Night one. Your warehouse app pushes item dot shipped: one POST.

cues.text: Sparrow stores it and answers in the same breath: 201, event ID.
Same parcel pushed twice? Same idempotency key, same event, no duplicate.
Then fan-out: every subscription that matches, by name, consumer, even labels like region=eu.
cues.say: Then fan-out: every subscription that matches, by name, consumer, even labels like region equals E-U.

cues.text: For each match, one request: your envelope or your own template, secret headers encrypted at rest, any HTTP method.
Signed, and out the door. Three parcels, three docks, three green ticks.
On the other side, your customer checks the signature.
One file to copy in: Python, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, and five more.
Wrong key, replayed, or older than five minutes? Rejected at the door.
Night two. 3:12 a.m. The partner's dock is closed: 503.
cues.say: Night two. Three twelve A-M. The partner's dock is closed: five-oh-three.

cues.text: Sparrow reads the answer. Server error? Worth another try. DNS, TLS, 4xx? It stops.
cues.say: Sparrow reads the answer. Server error? Worth another try. DNS, TLS, four-hundreds? It stops.

cues.text: So it backs off: one minute, two, four, doubling, capped at a day.
A 429 with Retry-After? It waits exactly that long, and it doesn't count as an attempt.
cues.say: A four twenty-nine with Retry-After? It waits exactly that long, and it doesn't count as an attempt.

cues.text: Fail after fail, the webhook's health slides: healthy, degraded, unhealthy.
Five in a row, and your on-call gets an email. You? You're asleep.
6:40. The partner is back. Every failed delivery from tonight: one snapshot, one retry.
cues.say: Six forty. The partner is back. Every failed delivery from tonight: one snapshot, one retry.

cues.text: A snapshot, not a live query: what you saw is exactly what gets retried.
And every attempt is on record: status, timing, category. Nothing is a mystery.
Night three. Tuesday's deploy put the wrong weight on every parcel.
Fix the bug. Then re-push every item.shipped from Tuesday: one snapshot, one job.
cues.say: Fix the bug. Then re-push every item dot shipped from Tuesday: one snapshot, one job.

cues.text: Partner mid-deploy? Pause their webhook. Deliveries wait. Resume when they're ready.
And your customers watch all of it themselves, in a portal you hand them with one link.
What goes out is yours to shape. A Go template turns the envelope into whatever the receiver expects.
Add your own headers, even an API token, encrypted at rest. Any method: POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
So one event can call almost any HTTP API, not just a webhook.
Recipes are those templates, pre-built: PagerDuty, Twilio, SendGrid, ClickHouse and more, one YAML file each.
One command: sparrow use pagerduty.
A dashboard ships inside the same binary: webhooks, events, deliveries, health.
And OpenTelemetry traces every parcel, push to dock.
So what does it need to run?
Just PostgreSQL. The queue lives there too. No Redis, no broker.
MIT licensed: free to run, fork and ship. No per-message pricing.
How does that stack up?
Svix and Convoy add Redis. Hookdeck's core is SaaS.
Sparrow is fully MIT, with dual signing, recipes, a portal and self-monitoring.
So, where did item.shipped end up?
cues.say: So, where did item dot shipped end up?

cues.text: Every dock. Every time. Even the nights you slept.
Push once. Sparrow does the rest.
One Go binary. One Postgres.
docker compose up, and you're delivering.
cues.say: Docker compose up, and you're delivering.
